clue.text: Go over a board that may be defied

parts.note: to comb an area is to go over it thoroughly
taken as written
a table is a board, as in board and lodging or a board meeting's table

explanation.surface: Someone checks a committee whose rulings might be challenged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something combatable can be fought against or opposed, so it is open to being defied.

clue.text: Grants to obtain: ball-points

parts.note: a ball is round, giving the letter O
W, N and S are compass points: west, north and south

explanation.surface: Someone is allowed to acquire a supply of ballpoint pens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grants' is a verb here, in the sense of concedes or admits; 'to obtain' is only link material joining it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up to something is to admit or concede it, the sense of grants as in 'I grant you that'.

clue.text: Gamble with a Greek character

parts.note: to gamble is to bet
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone places a wager alongside a man from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: The second letter of the Greek alphabet, following alpha.

clue.text: The company tore up letters in error

indicators.note: the letters of the words that precede are set out wrongly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A business destroyed some correspondence by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A troupe is a company of touring performers such as actors or dancers.

clue.text: He was arresting man in days gone by

definitions.text: He was arresting man in days gone by

parts.words: He was arresting man in days gone by
parts.note: 'arresting' seems to mean striking, but read literally it describes an early London police officer attached to a magistrates' court in the eighteenth century

explanation.surface: A man who was once very striking.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bow Street Runners were London's first professional police force, founded in the 1740s and attached to the Bow Street magistrates' court.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a member of an old London police force who made arrests.

clue.text: Finished after a top journalist went round'

indicators.note: the word for finished is placed after the journalist's letters

parts.note: the editor is the top journalist on a paper, abbreviated ED
to have died is to be finished

explanation.surface: Someone completed a task once a senior writer had done the rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that eddied swirled in a circle, so it went round.

clue.text: Swindle involving stone building in attractive surroundings

indicators.note: the attractive word forms the surroundings, with the remaining letters placed in it

parts.note: dishy is informal for attractive

indicators.note: building means the letters of stone are put together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A con involving putting up a stone building in a pretty setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' rearranges the stone, and 'surroundings' puts the result inside a British slang word for good-looking; 'involving' and 'in' are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonesty is deceitful behaviour, the quality behind any swindle or fraud.

clue.text: A good manone getting the drink!

parts.note: a good man is a saint, ST, and one is I; the OCR has run man and one together

explanation.surface: A virtuous fellow is the one who gets to have the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine from Piedmont, a drink.

clue.text: The piles made by pugilists?

parts.note: boxers have fights, informally scraps, so heaps of these fights would be what pugilists produce

explanation.surface: Boxers leave behind stacks of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrap heaps are piles of discarded junk, reread as heaps of scraps, meaning fights.

clue.text: Changes In diet now, a requisite throughout the country

indicators.note: changes means the letters that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Altering what we eat is now necessary across the whole nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requisite' is surface padding acting as a link between the anagram and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nationwide means extending over a whole nation, everywhere in the land.

clue.text: Expert artist backed by the church

indicators.note: backed means the artist's letters are read backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
CH is an abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A skilled painter has the support of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch can mean chief or principal, as in an arch-rival, hence expert.

clue.text: Just aiming to be blonde

parts.note: fair hair is blonde
to be minded to do something is to aim or intend to do it

explanation.surface: Someone merely wants to have light-coloured hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'merely' but is the adjective meaning impartial.
explanation.definitionFit: A just person is impartial, judging others even-handedly.

clue.text: The person observing a quarter idle away their. 'time

parts.note: S, south, is a quarter of the compass
to potter is to pass time idly on small tasks

explanation.surface: Someone watching a district lazes the hours away.
explanation.definitionFit: A spotter is someone who watches for and notes things, like a trainspotter or plane spotter.

clue.text: A composer composing in tears.

indicators.note: composing means arranging, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A songwriter is crying while working on a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: John Stainer was a Victorian English composer of church music, best known for The Crucifixion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Stainer was an English composer and organist.

clue.text: Touching spring produces a reaction

parts.note: re means concerning or touching on
a bound is a leap or spring

explanation.surface: Pressing on a coil makes it push back.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebound is a recoil or response, as in reacting after a setback.

clue.text: Virtuous aspiration in a certain class

indicators.note: in places the aspiration inside the word for class

parts.note: a caste is a hereditary social class
an aspirate is an H sound, the breathy letter

explanation.surface: Moral ambitions found within one social group.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure and abstaining, hence morally virtuous.

clue.text: The approach about defence is reassuring

indicators.note: about means the word for approach is placed around the other piece

parts.note: the coming of something is its approach
a fort is a defensive building

explanation.surface: The way a team defends is encouraging to its fans.
explanation.definitionFit: Something comforting soothes and consoles, giving reassurance.

clue.text: Strengthen a river enclosure

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a pen is an enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: Reinforcing a fenced area by the water.
explanation.definitionFit: To deepen feelings or colour is to intensify them, making them stronger.

clue.text: Union conveners.

parts.note: 'Union' suggests a trade union, and its conveners are shop stewards, but the union here is a wedding and those who arrange it are matchmakers

explanation.definitionFit: Such people arrange marriages, bringing couples together into a union.

clue.text: A guy who's evil or best

indicators.note: to best is to beat or overcome, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A man who is the best at being wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver is a man's first name, so it can stand for a guy.

clue.text: Account for the noise.

definitions.meaning: a loud bang, such as from a gun

explanation.definitionFit: A report is both a description of events and the sharp sound of a shot.

clue.text: See about game-sharp!

indicators.note: about means the word for see goes around the game

parts.note: to spy is to see
nap is a card game, short for napoleon

explanation.surface: Watch a game being played with real flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy means brisk or quick-witted, as in a sharp remark.

clue.text: Strict minister's retirement in view

indicators.note: in places the minister's letters inside the word for view

parts.note: to see is to view

indicators.note: retirement suggests going backwards, so the minister's letters are read in reverse

parts.note: REV is short for Reverend, a minister

explanation.surface: A clergyman takes a hard line on the prospect of stepping down.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe means harsh or stern, applying rules strictly.

clue.text: Supposed to. propose cutting the tall grass

indicators.note: cutting means the proposal piece goes into the grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass growing in water
to put a motion is to propose it

explanation.surface: Someone is expected to suggest mowing the long grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reputed is generally believed or assumed to be so.

clue.text: Put in order that's quite considerable

definitions.meaning: to arrange neatly, as a room
a sizeable amount, as a large sum of money

explanation.definitionFit: Tidy is both a verb for making neat and informal for a fairly large amount.

clue.text: Some artiste thinking, to be retained

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A performer has some thoughts and wants them kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet is the proofreader's mark meaning let it stand, so the text is kept.

clue.text: Pop in, causing distress

parts.note: pop and pa both mean father

explanation.surface: Dropping by causes someone upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain is suffering, physical or mental distress.

clue.text: Plant on a tip. site possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Greenery dumped on a rubbish site.
explanation.walkthrough: A tip is British for a rubbish dump.
explanation.definitionFit: A poinsettia is a plant with red bracts popular at Christmas.

clue.text: Out of gear

parts.note: sounds like a car not in gear, but gear means clothing and someone out of it is wearing none

explanation.definitionFit: Someone without any clothes on is naked.

clue.text: People in a rocky situation sound harrowing

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill or outcrop
men are people
a ting is a light ringing sound

explanation.surface: Climbers on a crag make a distressing noise.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky peak, found especially on Dartmoor in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tormenting causes great distress, as harrowing does.
